title: Pronouns — わたし／彼／彼女
summary: Pronouns stand in for people. Common ones are わたし (I), あなた (you), 彼 (he) and 彼女 (she). They are used with particles like は and の. Japanese often leaves them out when the context is clear.

patterns.gloss: 彼女は医者です (She is a doctor)

body.p: わたし (I), あなた (you), 彼 (he), 彼女 (she). 彼 and 彼女 can also mean “boyfriend / girlfriend”, so use the person’s name when you want to be clear.
は marks the topic (わたしは毎日歩きます), の shows possession (彼はわたしの友だちです).
Japanese does not always say “I” or “you”. If the subject is clear, it is dropped. Also, あなた is not used much to address a person; people use the name + さん.

examples.ja: 彼女（かのじょ）は 医者（いしゃ）です。
彼（かれ）はわたしの友（とも）だちです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa watashi no tomodachi desu.

examples.ja: わたしは毎日（まいにち）歩（ある）きます。

pitfalls: Do not call someone あなた to their face too often; use their name + さん.
彼 / 彼女 can mean boyfriend / girlfriend. Use the person’s name when unsure.
